# Privathospitalerne

**Privathospitalerne** ("the private hospitals") is the collective term, in the Danish ADHD quality database report for the period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025, for private hospital providers treating children and young people undergoing ADHD assessment [^src1]. The entity appears in the report's discussion of two national quality indicators — Indikator 2b, which measures how often a manualized diagnostic interview or environmental observation is carried out, and Indikator 3, which measures how often diagnostic conferences with specialist physicians are held [^src1].

The report singles out Privathospitalerne for a sharp decline in performance. On Indikator 2b, the private hospitals achieved a compliance rate of just 7%, down from 84% the previous year [^src1]. The report explicitly flags this as "en væsentlig lavere målopfyldelse" (a significantly lower goal achievement) compared with the year before [^src1]. On Indikator 3, the private hospitals' performance was even starker: of 16 registered treatment courses (forløb) recorded at private hospitals, none met the indicator — a 0% compliance rate [^src1].

The report cautions that these figures rest on a narrow data foundation ("det smalle datagrundlag") [^src1], meaning the small number of registered cases (16 in total for Indikator 3) makes the percentages statistically fragile and potentially misleading as a measure of overall private-hospital quality. This caveat sits within a broader national picture in which both indicators are substantially underperforming a 90% development target — 51% compliance nationally on Indikator 2b and 27% on Indikator 3 — with notable regional variation, including a positive trend in Region Midtjylland and a declining trend in Region Syddanmark [^src1]. In response to criticism of the existing indicators, the steering group behind the database has revised both Indikator 2b and Indikator 3 to better reflect current clinical practice and to allow for graduation of effort based on case complexity [^src1].
